customers.description: This table contains detailed information about each customer, including their contact details, country, and signup date.

categories.description: This table contains a master list of all available categories, each identified by a unique ID and name.

suppliers.description: This table lists all suppliers, including their unique identifiers, names, and countries of origin.

products.description: This table stores detailed information about all products offered, including their prices and categories.

orders.description: This table contains individual customer order details, including a unique order identifier, the associated customer, the date the order was placed, and its current fulfillment status.

order_items.description: This table contains details for each individual item included in customer orders, specifying the product, quantity, and unit price.

stg_orders.sql:
/* transformations.sql */ /* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */ /* These are "transformation models", the kind of layered SQL views you'd */ /* find in a real warehouse (think dbt staging -> intermediate -> mart */ /* layers). Each one builds on base tables and/or earlier views, which is */ /* exactly what creates the multi-hop "lineage graph" we want to extract. */ /* Layers: */ /*   staging     : stg_*           -> light cleanup of raw tables */ /*   facts/dims  : fct_*, dim_*     -> joined, business-friendly tables */ /*   marts       : everything else  -> aggregated, analysis-ready tables */ /* ---------------------------------------------------------------------- */ /* ===================== STAGING LAYER ===================== */ /* 1. Clean orders: drop cancelled orders, normalize date */
CREATE VIEW stg_orders AS
SELECT
  order_id,
  customer_id,
  order_date,
  status
FROM orders
WHERE
  status <> 'cancelled'
stg_orders.description: This view provides a foundational, lightly transformed set of order records, intended for downstream analytical models.

stg_order_items.sql:
/* 2. Clean order items: precompute line-level revenue */
CREATE VIEW stg_order_items AS
SELECT
  order_item_id,
  order_id,
  product_id,
  quantity,
  unit_price,
  quantity * unit_price AS line_total
FROM order_items
stg_order_items.description: This view contains cleaned order item details including the calculated line-level revenue for each item in an order.

dim_customers.sql:
/* 3. Customer dimension: add a derived "segment" based on signup date */
CREATE VIEW dim_customers AS
SELECT
  customer_id,
  name,
  email,
  country,
  signup_date,
  CASE WHEN signup_date < '2023-01-01' THEN 'legacy' ELSE 'new' END AS customer_segment
FROM customers
dim_customers.description: This view provides core customer information, including a derived segment based on their signup date.

dim_products.sql:
/* 4. Product dimension: denormalize category + supplier info */
CREATE VIEW dim_products AS
SELECT
  p.product_id,
  p.name AS product_name,
  p.price,
  c.name AS category_name,
  s.name AS supplier_name,
  s.country AS supplier_country
FROM products AS p
JOIN categories AS c
  ON p.category_id = c.category_id
JOIN suppliers AS s
  ON p.supplier_id = s.supplier_id
dim_products.description: This view provides a comprehensive, denormalized list of all products, including their category and supplier information.

fct_order_revenue.sql:
/* ===================== FACT LAYER ===================== */ /* 5. Order-level revenue: join cleaned orders with cleaned line items */
CREATE VIEW fct_order_revenue AS
SELECT
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_date,
  SUM(oi.line_total) AS order_revenue
FROM stg_orders AS o
JOIN stg_order_items AS oi
  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY
  o.order_id,
  o.customer_id,
  o.order_date
fct_order_revenue.description: This view aggregates order line items to calculate the total revenue for each order, including customer and order date information.

product_sales_summary.sql:
/* 6. Product sales summary: combine cleaned line items with product dimension */
CREATE VIEW product_sales_summary AS
SELECT
  oi.product_id,
  dp.product_name,
  dp.category_name,
  dp.supplier_name,
  SUM(oi.quantity) AS units_sold,
  SUM(oi.line_total) AS total_revenue
FROM stg_order_items AS oi
JOIN dim_products AS dp
  ON oi.product_id = dp.product_id
GROUP BY
  oi.product_id,
  dp.product_name,
  dp.category_name,
  dp.supplier_name
product_sales_summary.description: This view provides a summarized overview of product sales, including units sold and total revenue, along with product details such as category and supplier.

customer_lifetime_value.sql:
/* ===================== MART LAYER ===================== */ /* 7. Customer lifetime value: combine order revenue with customer dimension */
CREATE VIEW customer_lifetime_value AS
SELECT
  f.customer_id,
  d.name,
  d.country,
  d.customer_segment,
  SUM(f.order_revenue) AS lifetime_value,
  COUNT(f.order_id) AS total_orders
FROM fct_order_revenue AS f
JOIN dim_customers AS d
  ON f.customer_id = d.customer_id
GROUP BY
  f.customer_id,
  d.name,
  d.country,
  d.customer_segment
customer_lifetime_value.description: This view provides the lifetime value and total orders for each customer, along with their key demographic and segment information.

category_revenue.sql:
/* 8. Revenue by category */
CREATE VIEW category_revenue AS
SELECT
  category_name,
  SUM(total_revenue) AS category_revenue,
  SUM(units_sold) AS category_units
FROM product_sales_summary
GROUP BY
  category_name
category_revenue.description: This view provides the total revenue and units sold for each product category.

supplier_performance.sql:
/* 9. Supplier performance */
CREATE VIEW supplier_performance AS
SELECT
  supplier_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS product_count,
  SUM(total_revenue) AS supplier_revenue
FROM product_sales_summary
GROUP BY
  supplier_name
supplier_performance.description: This view aggregates sales data to provide key performance metrics for each supplier, including product count and total revenue.

monthly_revenue.sql:
/* 10. Monthly revenue trend */
CREATE VIEW monthly_revenue AS
SELECT
  STRFTIME('%Y-%m', order_date) AS month,
  SUM(order_revenue) AS monthly_revenue,
  COUNT(order_id) AS order_count
FROM fct_order_revenue
GROUP BY
  month
monthly_revenue.description: This view provides a monthly summary of total revenue and the corresponding number of orders.

customer_country_revenue.sql:
/* 11. Revenue by customer country */
CREATE VIEW customer_country_revenue AS
SELECT
  country,
  SUM(lifetime_value) AS country_revenue,
  COUNT(customer_id) AS customer_count
FROM customer_lifetime_value
GROUP BY
  country
customer_country_revenue.description: This view provides the total revenue and customer count broken down by country.

top_customers.sql:
/* 12. Top customers by lifetime value */
CREATE VIEW top_customers AS
SELECT
  customer_id,
  name,
  country,
  lifetime_value,
  total_orders
FROM customer_lifetime_value
WHERE
  lifetime_value > 100
ORDER BY
  lifetime_value DESC
top_customers.description: This view identifies high-value customers based on their lifetime value and total orders, filtering for those with a lifetime value greater than 100.

repeat_customers.sql:
/* 13. Repeat customers (more than one order) */
CREATE VIEW repeat_customers AS
SELECT
  customer_id,
  name,
  total_orders
FROM customer_lifetime_value
WHERE
  total_orders > 1
repeat_customers.description: This view lists customers who have placed more than one order, along with their names and total order counts.

avg_order_value_by_segment.sql:
/* 14. Average order value by customer segment */
CREATE VIEW avg_order_value_by_segment AS
SELECT
  customer_segment,
  AVG(lifetime_value * 1.0 / total_orders) AS avg_order_value
FROM customer_lifetime_value
GROUP BY
  customer_segment
avg_order_value_by_segment.description: This view calculates the average order value for each customer segment based on their lifetime value.

category_supplier_matrix.sql:
/* 15. Category x supplier matrix */
CREATE VIEW category_supplier_matrix AS
SELECT
  category_name,
  supplier_name,
  COUNT(*) AS product_count
FROM dim_products
GROUP BY
  category_name,
  supplier_name
category_supplier_matrix.description: A cross-reference matrix showing how many products each supplier provides within each product category.
